descriptionChirho: A person related by blood or family ties; a kinsman or kinswoman. All four auto-clustered senses represent the same core meaning of familial relationship, differing only in grammatical number (singular vs. plural) and case inflection. The glosses across all occurrences are virtually identical: Arabic أَقارِب/نَسِيب, German Verwandte, Hebrew קְרוֹבִים, Korean 친척/친족, Spanish parientes. Whether used of Elizabeth as Mary's relative (Lk 1:36), the relatives who rejoiced at John's birth (Lk 1:58), Cornelius gathering his relatives (Acts 10:24), or Paul's kinsmen in Romans 9:3 and 16:7-21, the semantic content is uniform. The 'kinsmen' label in Romans reflects Paul's ethnic-national kinship, but the underlying lexical sense remains 'relative by blood.'
